objective.statement: Use a two-beat rest for half of a four-beat bar, but never for the middle two beats.
successCriteria: I know a two-beat rest may fill the first or the second half of a bar of four beats.
I know a two-beat rest must not cover beats 2 and 3.
I can fix a bar that breaks this rule.

explanation.text: In a bar of four beats (4/4 or 4/2), the bar divides into two halves: beats 1 and 2, and beats 3 and 4.
A rest of two beats may fill one of these halves. It may not start on beat 2, because it would cross the middle of the bar and hide beat 3.

music.textAlternative: One bar of 4/4: two crotchets then a minim rest.

explanation.caption: Right: a minim rest fills the second half of the bar (beats 3 and 4).

music.textAlternative: One bar of 4/4: a crotchet, two crotchet rests, a crotchet.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: crotchet, crotchet rest, crotchet rest, crotchet.

explanation.caption: Right: beats 2 and 3 are silent, so each gets its own crotchet rest.

explanation.text: A single minim rest in the middle, on beats 2 and 3, is the mistake to avoid. In 4/2 the same rule holds, with a semibreve rest for two minim beats.
Look at the middle of the bar. A two-beat rest must start on beat 1 or beat 3, never on beat 2.

music.textAlternative: One bar of 4/4: a minim rest, then two crotchets.

steps: Beats 1 and 2 are silent, the first half of the bar.
One minim rest fills that half neatly.
